newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on weather and crop factors.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on weather and crop factors.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed lower on forecasts for rain in European wheat growing areas, talk recent winterkill damage in the U.S. Great Plains wasn't as bad as expected, and improved weather prospects in the U.S. wheat growing areas, traders said.
"We were just swamped, very volatile and very busy," a trader said.

The market attempted to rally in late dealings on news the EU slapped a tax on daily exports of soft wheat to conserve domestic supplies. Dry weather in Europe has led to concerns about wheat production shortfalls.
But the widespread talk in late trading that recent freeze damage to the U.S. hard red winter crop wasn't as bad as some had expected rekindled selling interest, the traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 76.890 million bushels, above the 36.920 million traded Wednesday.
KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed 14-3/4 to 21 cents per bushel lower, with May down 15-1/2 at $4.68. July was down 16-1/2 at $4.45.
